newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Heavy surges on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Heavy surges on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Shares of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd surged in Monday afternoon trade, as investors were relieved that a research institute had decided not to alter the company's rating, brokers said.

By 0339 GMT, the shares had risen 59 yen to 824. Turnover totalled 6.004 million, making Mitsubishi the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse. It was also the second largest percentage gainer.
Nomura Research Institute said on Friday it had decided to keep Mitsubishi Heavy's rating at a "2", encouraging investors to bargain-hunt, brokers said.
The shares had been under heavy selling pressure after Nomura Resesearch Institute lowered the rating to a "2" from a "1" in February.

The company is expected to be hurt by falling prices of power plant equipment and environment-related equipment, Nomura Research said. It may also be negatively affected by possible cuts in capital outlay by electric utility companies amid growing public criticism of utility charges.
Selling of its shares accelerated last week following an accident at a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant, pushing it well below the 800 yen line.
